newsitem.title: ITALY: Large group of Albanians arrives in Italy by boat.
newsitem.headline: Large group of Albanians arrives in Italy by boat.

text.p: A group of some 50 Albanians fleeing violence in the south of their country arrived in Italy by boat on Friday, Italian television and radio reported.
RAI state television said a twin-masted fishing boat was intercepted by coastguards some 25 miles to the north of the Italian port Otranto and escorted into the harbour.
It said 15 women and 11 children on board had been transferred from the boat earlier and brought to land by coastguards.
The Italian news agency ANSA, however, reported that a total of 47 people -- 24 men, 11 women and 12 children -- were on the boat.
One woman was quoted as saying that all were family or friends from the southern Albanian port of Vlore, where rioting broke out last week and the government has lost control.
She said the group left at around 7.30 p.m. on Thursday after watching Italian news bulletins.
"We saw the latest news and reports of tanks heading for Vlore and were afraid," she was quoted as saying.
A radio reporter in Otranto said the Albanians were being held in converted containers in the port, which lies a short distance across the Adriatic from Vlore.
Italy said on Thursday it would repatriate all Albanians entering the country illegally.

"If we had to decide with our hearts, of course, we would let these Albanian citizens stay in Italy, but this would mean opening the doors to everyone, local government official Giuseppe Mazzitello told reporters on Thursday.
He said then that a group of 29 Albanians, including nine children, who arrived on a motorboat in Otranto on Wednesday would probably be sent back by ferry to Durres.
Otranto usually has a ferry to Vlore but links have been cut due to the violence that has swept southern Albania.
Italy organised an airlift of its citizens and foreign reporters from Vlore earlier in the week.
The authorities have stepped up patrols to prevent a wave of immigrants trying to make the Adriatic crossing.
Tens of thousands of Albanians made a mass exodus to Italy in 1991 after 45 years of Stalinist rule crumbled.
